# Performance Characteristics

Dimension covering OPA policy evaluation latency, memory footprint, cold start,
and benchmarks. Sources: [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Latency

### Official Targets

OPA documentation states a 1ms budget for microservice API authorization use
cases [2].

### Benchmarking Tools

- `opa bench`: reports ns/op, B/op, allocs/op, histogram at 90/95/99/99.9/99.99
  percentiles [2]
- `opa test --bench`: benchmarks unit tests, supports `--benchmem` and `--count` [2]

### Measured Performance

| Scenario | Latency | Source |
|---|---|---|
| RBAC policy evaluation (profiler) | 237.126µs total [2] | Official docs |
| Optimized zip code lookup | 8µs [46] | Styra blog |
| Sidecar deployment | 2-5ms per decision (est. from search snippets — full article inaccessible) | Styra blog [27] |
| RBAC per-rule costs | 3.167µs - 25.75µs [2] | Official docs |

### Regorus Comparison

| Engine | Mean ± Std Dev | Runs | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regorus (Rust) | 4.6ms ± 0.2ms | 422 | ACI policy [9] |
| OPA (Go) | 45.2ms ± 0.6ms | 62 | ACI policy [9] |

Methodology: hyperfine, query `data.framework.mount_overlay=x` [9].
This represents a ~10x speedup but uses a specific ACI policy — performance
ratios may differ for API authorization policies.

## Memory Footprint

### Scaling Rules

| Input | Memory | Multiplier | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8MB JSON (100k objects) | ~160MB RAM | 20x | [2] |
| 10,000 rules | ~130MB RAM | — | [2] |
| 100,000 rules | ~1.1GB RAM | — | [2] |
| Raw JSON to OPA data structures (not total RAM) | — | 6x | [30] |

The official documentation states total memory consumption is "approximately 20x more"
than the serialized format on disk [2]. Note: the 6x multiplier from [30] measures
OPA's internal data structure overhead only, while the 20x from [2] measures total
RAM including indexing and runtime overhead.

### Production Failures

At extreme scale, users have reported [31]:
- 20-30k policies: 100% CPU, 5GB+ memory, 10-30s response times

These are user-reported from GitHub issues, not controlled benchmarks.

## Bundle Loading (Cold Start)

Bundle loading times scale **non-linearly** [30]:

| Bundle Size | Load Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 100MB | 16s | Baseline |
| 200MB | 71s | 4.4x time for 2x size |
| 500MB | 690s | 43x time for 5x size |

Root cause: 95%+ of allocations come from recursive data merging [30].
This represents a structural limitation in OPA's data loading architecture.

## WASM Performance

WASM performance is **mixed** relative to native Rego [29]:

| Scenario | Rego | WASM | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5000 rules (no indexing) | 1229ms | 2740ms | Rego (2.2x) |
| 200 rules (with indexing) | ~23,882 ns/op | ~95,528 ns/op (calculated from 23,882 × 4) | Rego (4x) |

OPA's integration docs describe WASM as "Fastest" [4], but this appears to be
aspirational rather than universally true. Rego's indexing optimizations do not
apply to WASM, which explains the discrepancy [29].

## Optimization Techniques

### Rule Indexing

OPA's linear fragment provides "near constant time" evaluation [2]:
- Equality statements: `input.x == "foo"` (indexed), `input.x[i] == "foo"` (not indexed)
- Glob patterns: `glob.match("foo:*:bar", ...)` (indexed), patterns with `**` (not indexed)

### Early Exit

Evaluation halts after first match for complete document rules with single
ground values — common in `allow` rules [2].

### Comprehension Indexing

Prevents O(n²) complexity in group-by operations by computing and memoizing
collection values once [2].

### Objects vs Arrays

Objects with unique identifiers enable O(1) lookups vs O(n) array searching [2].

### Storage Optimization

`--optimize-store-for-read-speed` precomputes AST representation during writes,
eliminating runtime conversion overhead. Trade-off: slower writes, increased
memory footprint [2].

### Partial Evaluation

Pre-compiles policies at build time [2]:
- `-O=1`: partially evaluates rules not depending on unknowns, inlines known values
- `-O=2`: additionally inlines virtual documents, copy propagation

## Gaps and Limitations

- No official p50/p90/p99 latency percentiles for HTTP API authorization
  specifically (Envoy performance page returned 404)
- Cold start timing for realistic data volumes (1-100MB) not well-characterized
  beyond the non-linear bundle loading data [30]
- WASM vs Rego decision matrix (when to use which) not available from official
  sources
- Production deployment latency distributions across industries not published
- GC tuning guidance (GOGC values, trade-offs) not found in official docs
- All alternative engine performance claims are vendor-sourced without
  independent verification
